name: Level-Five Technique
reason: The adaptation replaced the source novel's qualitative technique-grade labels (e.g. 'Saint Class' secret manuals) with a simple numeric tier system; 'Level-Five Technique' is the top tier in that scheme.
description: The highest grade in the show's technique-ranking system. Titan Strike is identified in Ep 92 as a Level-Five Technique, the only one of its kind known to the Skyreach Sect.

name: Violet Pulse Energy
reason: The source term 'Purple Sandalwood Genuine Qi' (from the Luo Family's Purple Sandalwood Fist) was localized as 'Violet Pulse Energy' to fit the Western fantasy register, with the parent technique renamed 'Violet Pulse'.
description: The energy produced by cultivating the Violet Pulse technique. In Ep 95 the Violet Pulse Energy flooding Zane's system is steadily consumed to build up Nether Essence inside him, mirroring source ch. 81 where the Heavenly Devil Genuine Qi devours Luo Zheng's Purple Sandalwood Genuine Qi.

name: Elder Phoenix Gem
reason: No corresponding item appears in the aligned source auction chapters; the gem appears to be an adaptation-created rarity named for the Western fantasy setting.
description: An extremely rare gem offered at the auction in Ep 97; Dustin could not remember the last time an Elder Phoenix Gem had hit the market.

name: Sky-sunder Axe
reason: No matching axe appears in the aligned source auction chapters (chs ~83-86); the weapon appears to be an adaptation-created auction lot with a Western fantasy name.
description: A genuine Soul Armament axe auctioned in Eps 97-98. Despite its unwieldy, unrefined appearance it ultimately fetched a staggering five thousand Crystal Cubes, drawing gasps from the auction hall.

name: Argent-Gold Demon Peak
reason: The source's unwieldy 'Gold Silver Demonic Spring Mountain' was compressed to 'Argent-Gold Demon Peak' for a cleaner Western fantasy name.
description: A mountain used as a strength trial: all attacks landed on the Argent-Gold Demon Peak are recorded and ranked (Ep 1112, matching source ch. 1092 where a screen records the attacks the Gold Silver Demonic Spring Mountain has borne).

name: Gossamer Token
reason: The source's 'Lingyan Jade Token' (from the Lingyan Pavilion) was localized as 'Gossamer Token', rendering the 'Lingyan' (silken mist) image in English.
description: A token issued by the Lingyan Pavilion's localized counterpart that lets its bearer travel the Alliance's great worlds free of charge. Zane keeps his ready at cross-realm checkpoints, though in Ep 1116 the guards wave him through without even checking it, exactly as in source ch. 1096.

name: Thirty-six Halls
reason: Source term 'thirty-six halls' (of the Lingwu Holy Place) was carried over directly as 'Thirty-six Halls' for the Western fantasy setting.
description: The thirty-six regional halls of the Soulbound Sect's holy land, each governing a thousand great cities (source ch. 1001). Their Hall Masters are peak figures regionally, but as noted in Ep 1028, in The Holy City the Thirty-six Halls are nothing compared to the major factions.

name: Twilight Bloom Hall
reason: The source's 'Xu Hua Palace' (a hall of the Spirit Martial Holy Land run by Hall Master Shen) was renamed 'Twilight Bloom Hall' to fit the Western fantasy register.
description: One of the Thirty-six Halls, run by hall master Sloan (source: Hall Master Shen). Zane stays there over two weeks in Ep 1123, and Freya easily gathers information there, matching source ch. 1103 where information is easy to find in the Xu Hua Palace.

name: Malachi
issues: Split localization: the same source figure (Empyrean Original Sin / Original Sin Heavenly Lord) is called 'Malachi' in Eps 671 and 1124 but reverts to the literal title 'Supreme Lord of Original Sin' in Eps 1199 and 1216.
reason: The source title-name 'Empyrean Original Sin' was localized to the personal name 'Malachi', a biblical-sounding name befitting an ancient god-like faction leader.
description: Leader of the largest of the human race's three great factions in the upper world, commanding four thousand realms (Ep 671, matching Empyrean Original Sin in source ch. 652); his long-running conflict with Lumen (Empyrean Oracle) divides humanity. Long ago he spent one hundred thousand years collecting the Faith Energy of trillions of living beings to hatch a sword embryo, now ranked second on the Cosmic Spirit Index (Ep 1124, matching the Original Sin Heavenly Lord in source ch. 1104).

name: Zane’s Storage Ring
reason: Possessive mention of Zane's own Storage Ring, the spatial storage device already tracked in the master sheet.

name: Eternal Night World
reason: Source term 'Eternal Night World' was carried over unchanged, already fitting the Western fantasy register.
description: A world that once belonged to the King of Slaughter and was purged after his disappearance (source chs. 1108-1109). In Ep 1129 Nyla makes an excuse to leave and, carrying the runestone Lavender gave her, sets off for the Eternal Night World - matching Ling Lan's journey with Xun's jade slip in the source.

name: Demon Energy Holy Land
reason: Source term 'Demon Energy Holy Land' (in the Yin Luo World) was retained verbatim in the adaptation.
description: A holy land of the Demon Clan (localized as the Ogre/Demon Clan faction) whose mountain-like Saint Lord watches the opening of the underground palace through a surveillance array and sends his top geniuses inside (Eps 1133 and 1140, matching source ch. 1113).

name: Lantern Pearl
reason: The source's 'Luminous Night Orb' was renamed 'Lantern Pearl', a more natural English image for a light-giving treasure.
description: A light-emitting pearl that serves as the party's only light in the suffocating darkness of the underground palace; in Ep 1135 it is swarmed by finger-sized black cannibal moths, matching the black moths that shoot at the Luminous Night Orb in source ch. 1115.

name: Soulbound Sect’s Saint Lord
reason: The source's 'Holy Lord' of the Lingwu (Spirit Martial) Holy Land was rendered via the localized institution name as the 'Soulbound Sect's Saint Lord'.
description: The supreme ruler of the Soulbound Sect back in the Psychean Realm. In Ep 1137 he is remembered as a figure Freya could once barely look up to, corresponding to the Spiritual Martial Sanctuary's Holy Lord whom even Luo Zheng could not refuse in the source.

name: Upper World Zane
reason: Extraction artifact concatenating the location 'Upper World' with 'Zane'; the mentions refer to Zane Lowell himself.

name: Snow World
reason: The source's 'Freezing Snow World' was shortened to 'Snow World' for the adaptation.
description: The frozen world that is home to the Snow Demons, shape-shifting vicious creatures that read a warrior's dearest memories and take that person's form to possess them (Ep 1150, matching source ch. 1131).

name: Pools of Faith
reason: Source term 'Faith Pool' (also rendered 'Pond of Faith') was localized as 'Pools of Faith' for the Western fantasy register.
description: The three sacred reservoirs of the Night clan that constantly absorb the faith energy of its trillions of citizens through the three king statues. They belong to the clan as a whole, and sealing one is a grave taboo (Eps 1157-1162, matching source chs. 1140-1141).

name: Mist Palace Yolande
reason: Extraction artifact concatenating her palace ('Mist Palace', source Misty Cloud Palace) with her name; the mentions refer to Yolande (source Yun Luo).

name: Cassian Taryn Maren and Paige
reason: Not an entity: a run-together list of four separate character names (Cassian, Taryn, Maren, Paige), each covered individually.

name: Six Paths of Reincarnation
reason: Source term 'Six Paths of Reincarnation' was retained verbatim, as the Buddhist-flavored cosmological concept still reads naturally in the Western fantasy setting.
description: The cycle through which life is reborn in the setting's cosmology (source chs. 538-1144). In Ep 1164 one character tells another, 'You entered the Six Paths of Reincarnation before me.'

name: Saint Lords’
reason: Possessive plural of the rank title 'Saint Lord'; not a distinct entity beyond the singular title already tracked.

name: Maren Taryn and Paige
reason: Not an entity: a run-together list of three separate character names (Maren, Taryn, Paige), each covered individually.

name: Exterminator
reason: The source enforcer's name 'Mie' (which means 'exterminate/destroy') was localized as the epithet 'Exterminator', translating the name's meaning rather than its sound.
description: An enforcer of the Night clan dispatched by the Queen of Punishment (source: Yao orders Mie and others sent to the Sifting Yin World in ch. 1141). He appears in Eps 1171-1174, aligned with Mie's appearances in source chs. 1148-1152.

name: Imperial Vigorite
reason: The source material 'Emperor's Soul Rock' was renamed 'Imperial Vigorite' to sound like a precious fantasy mineral.
description: An impossibly rare building material. In Ep 1173 Livingston, who has lived longer than some Supreme Lords and has only ever seen a palm-sized piece, is stunned to find an entire plaza of the immortal mansion paved with genuine Imperial Vigorite - matching Lianshenzi's discovery of the Emperor's Soul Rock floor in source ch. 1153.

name: Infinite Crystal Sword
reason: The source's 'Myriad Life Crystal Sword' was renamed 'Infinite Crystal Sword', preserving the endless-splitting concept in a tighter English name.
description: Maverick's crystal sword, drawn in his bid for the Crown of Destiny (Eps 1176-1177). Per source ch. 1157 it can split from one blade into two, two into four and so on with the wielder's strength, each copy as powerful as the first, and is ranked 2120 on the Cosmic Spirit Index.

name: Zane’s Roaring Token
reason: Possessive mention of Zane's own Roaring Token (source term 'Roaring Token', chs 968-1306).

name: Star of Golden Sand Zane
reason: Extraction artifact concatenating the location 'Star of Golden Sand' (source Yellowsand Star, chs 1160-1163) with 'Zane'; the mentions refer to Zane Lowell himself.

name: Spatial Transference
reason: Source term 'Spatial Transference' was retained verbatim as the standard name for short-range teleportation.
description: A teleportation ability used by high-realm warriors to move or escape instantly. In Ep 1188 even Supreme Lords find that Spatial Transference and secret escape techniques cannot carry them past the Melee's hundred-mile binding zone.

name: Melee
reason: The source's inconsistently translated 'Life Risking Melee' / 'Life Extinguishing Melee' / 'Desperate Melee' was simplified to 'the Melee' in the adaptation.
description: A karmic binding formation of the immortal mansion that Zane unintentionally triggered on first entering (Ep 1187, matching source ch. 1166). It locks all linked combatants - even Supreme Lords - inside a hundred-mile zone until the death match resolves, with the factions' colors tracking the balance of the fight.

name: Heroic Wife
reason: The source tale of the 'Yue Nu Wang Qing' - a wife avenging her framed husband - was localized as the legend 'The Heroic Wife'.
description: The most famous legend of Zane's home world, a tale told throughout the Union of Seven Divine Kingdoms about a wife who avenges her husband after he is framed by a scoundrel. In Ep 1191 Zane recites it word for word through the Roaring Token, matching the Yue Nu Wang Qing story in source ch. 1171.

name: Soul Sea Realm Gus
reason: Extraction artifact concatenating the cultivation stage 'Soul Sea Realm' with the character name 'Gus'; the mentions refer to Gus, the Master's second disciple fought in the trial (Eps 1194-1195).

name: Primeval Deathspirit Wood
reason: The source's 'Chaos Dead Spirit Wood' was renamed 'Primeval Deathspirit Wood' for a smoother Western fantasy compound.
description: A near-mythical wood requiring hundreds of millions of undisturbed years to grow, fed by burying warriors' corpses beneath it; even a Heavenly Venerable could scarcely cultivate one (Ep 1197, matching the Chaos Dead Spirit Wood in source ch. 1177).

name: Sun Spring Essence Flame
reason: The source's 'Yang Spring Essence Flame' was localized as 'Sun Spring Essence Flame', translating 'Yang' into its solar sense for Western listeners.
description: A rare essence flame encountered in Ep 1197, corresponding to the Yang Spring Essence Flame of source ch. 1177.

name: Supreme Lord of Original Sin
issues: Name drift / split entity: Eps 671 and 1124 localize this source figure (Empyrean Original Sin / Original Sin Heavenly Lord) as 'Malachi', but Eps 1199 and 1216 revert to the literal title 'Supreme Lord of Original Sin' - the leader of the Thoughtless Minds controlling four thousand Supreme Worlds, i.e. the same character.
reason: Literal rendering of the source title 'Empyrean Original Sin' used in later episodes where the established localized name 'Malachi' should have been used.

name: Imperial Slash
reason: The source saber technique 'Monarch Slash' was renamed 'Imperial Slash', keeping the regal connotation in the Western fantasy register.
description: A legendary swift and fierce slashing technique (source ch. 1185). In Ep 1205 even the Imperial Slash cannot so much as graze the fabric of Zane's clothes while he declines to fight back.

name: Berserk Blood
reason: Source term 'Berserk Blood' was retained verbatim; the race that bears it was localized from the demon race to the Ogre race.
description: A bloodline power of the Ogre race that lets a warrior briefly forget pain and double his strength at some cost to the body. In Ep 1209 Thane's Bronze Blood is described as a cousin of the Ogre race's Berserk Blood, matching source ch. 1189 where Bronze Blood amplifies more and harms less than the demon race's Berserk Blood.

name: Body Tempering
reason: Source term 'body tempering' was retained verbatim as the name of the physical-cultivation path.
description: The physical cultivation system, a complete martial path distinct from true-essence cultivation: the practitioner tempers the mortal body and its acupoints toward the Leakless True Body and the Pedestal realms (source ch. 465). Referenced in Ep 1210.

name: Tome of Abiding Past
reason: The source Buddhist scripture 'Past Solemnity Calamity' was renamed 'Tome of Abiding Past', keeping the 'past' motif in a more evocative English title.
description: A Buddhist scripture that is also a cultivation method, common in the Ten Thousand Buddha Sacred Realm of the source (ch. 1286). In the show it powers the four Dragon-Taming Sentinels of the ancient sanctuary, letting them endlessly regenerate (Eps 1222 and 1305, matching the Dragon Taming Arhats of source chs. 1200-1201), and in Ep 1306 Zane recognizes it as a cultivation method rather than a mere monastic text.
